terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js books places in data/kilnworth.db and shows the places left.

tasks.title: Keep bookings in a table of their own
tasks.description:
Change `createTables(db)` in `src/db.js` so it also makes a `bookings` table, unless the database already has it:

- `id`, the `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`
- `workshopId`, a whole number that must be the `id` of a row in `workshops`
- `name`, text

Neither `workshopId` nor `name` may be empty (`NULL`). The workshops table is made as before.

The check runs `createTables` on an empty database, looks at the columns and the link it made, adds bookings for a workshop that exists, for one that does not and without a name, and runs it a second time.
nextSteps: Add a second `CREATE TABLE` to the SQL in `createTables`.
Give it the three columns and say which cannot be empty.
Tell the database what `workshopId` refers to.
hints: One `db.exec` can run two statements when a `;` separates them, and each needs its own `IF NOT EXISTS`.
`REFERENCES workshops (id)` after a column's type makes it a foreign key: the database then refuses a value that is not the id of a workshop.
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bookings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, workshopId INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workshops (id), name TEXT NOT NULL)`.

tasks.title: Book a place
tasks.description:
Implement `book(workshopId, name)` in `src/store.js`.

- when a workshop has that id, it adds a row to `bookings` and returns `{ booking: { id, workshopId, name } }`, with the id the database gave the row
- when no workshop has that id, it adds nothing and returns `{ problem: 'not_found' }`

Each value reaches the database in the place of a `?`. The route in `src/routes/bookings.js` answers 201, or 404 for the problem.

The check sends `POST /bookings` for workshops of its own, one name with an apostrophe in it, and a workshop that is not there, then looks at the bookings table and the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Find out whether the workshop is there, and return the problem if it is not.
Write the `INSERT` for a booking with a `?` for each value.
Return the booking with the id from the result of `run()`.
hints: The store can already read one workshop by its id.
If the database refuses a booking for a missing workshop, that error reaches the error handler as a 500. Check first with `get(workshopId)`. `lastInsertRowid` is the id of the new row.

`if (!get(workshopId)) return { problem: 'not_found' }`, then `db.prepare('INSERT INTO bookings (workshopId, name) VALUES (?, ?)').run(workshopId, name)` and `return { booking: { id: lastInsertRowid, workshopId, name } }`.

tasks.title: Work out the places left
tasks.description:
Change `list` and `get` in `src/store.js` so each workshop comes back with one more field, `placesLeft`: its `seats` minus the number of its bookings.

- a workshop with no bookings is still there, with every place left
- the filters of `list` and the 404 of `get` work as before
- `placesLeft` comes back from the query, worked out by the database

The check fills a database of its own with workshops and bookings, reads single workshops and lists, and looks at the rows your queries give back.
nextSteps: Join the bookings to the workshops in the query of `get`.
Keep the workshops that have no bookings.
Count the bookings per workshop and take them from the seats.
Do the same in `list`, then run `node try.js`.
hints: With two tables in the query, a column such as `id` has to say which table it belongs to. Give each table a short name with `AS`.
`LEFT JOIN` keeps a workshop with no bookings. `COUNT(b.id)` counts only real bookings, `GROUP BY w.id` counts per workshop, and `AS placesLeft` names the result.

`SELECT w.id, w.title, w.day, w.seats, w.priceCents, w.seats - COUNT(b.id) AS placesLeft FROM workshops AS w LEFT JOIN bookings AS b ON b.workshopId = w.id`, then the `WHERE`, `GROUP BY w.id` and, in `list`, `ORDER BY w.id`.
